### 2026-11-03: # starting with a small jeep!

**1.7h**

# starting with a small jeep!

I'm planning to make my project in Blender, which may or may not be a mistake considering the time I have for the project, though I've wanted to learn Blender for the longest time! I started by following this guide for the car: https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=1n_lmuEQyZM

It's pretty helpful, not only in getting me to learn some of the basic functions of Blender (such as s for scale, ctrl + b for bevel, etc.), but I can also customize it pretty easily to make the actual body of the car.

![Screenshot 2026-11-03 001607](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/9dc7760ecde20eaaa00c71987460ded98f289ba80f9949f1b4e5b4c428de8130.png)

For example, one of the things I added was the seat in the back and having two elevated sections with a divot in the middle. Of course, with Blender, there are a few problems that arose, one of which was being that, when I tried to add in the wheels, I discovered that my car body was non-manifold.

![Screenshot 2026-11-03 002823](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/4b72d84e0f183389706a0980168dd8f7dbe398ce24aad6e92f8fa6b0558b5172.png)
I couldn't figure out why or how to fix it, and I tried pressing f to fill in but all it did was this:

![Screenshot 2026-11-03 010221](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/604244a1223d71f61dc37f3bd7214a5f3a397ce8b80bc0f08f8f6bc9b0b8e802.png)

It took me a long time, but I eventually just settled with using solidify to make the walls thicker and not just a flat 2D plane, but I'll try my best to finish some more tomorrow.

tl;dr is that I made the basic car body using a tutorial but customizing it to fit better with my vision

### 2026-11-04: # finishing up the jeep!

**2h**

# finishing up the jeep!

After a LOT of trouble of trying to figure out why my mesh was rendered as non-manifold, and even trying to fill in all the extra holes, I just can't figure it out :( I have no idea why it's like that or how to make it manifold, so I just decided to restart the model. It was a lot faster though, since I knew what I needed to do to make it. At first, I thought I would try just making it from memory, but I hated the outcome:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/0e0c80398ab44c63a521d2e8b1859fab8caa9425ad014bdb676124404b1fc471.png)
The proportions were just really wrong and I loved my first model, so for my second attempt I just recreated that with the same proportions. For some reason, this model rendered as manifold, but I have no idea why or what I did different from my first attempt. Though, with this, I was able to create the wheel holes! One of my biggest issues was Blender's inability to have a huge undo memory, and since every single action in Blender counts as something that can be undone (even selecting an item), you end up with a TON of actions. But, if you make a change you regret later on, you can't just undo it because Blender doesn't remember that much. It's super annoying and I had to restart my model many times.

![Screenshot 2026-11-03 224131](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/08d6b9a8a5f8dafe1ce7ed63018a5bdb12e491ea200853aa8ce7e31f616ff4f3.png)

And finally I added some details using some extruding and shapes to finish off the jeep!

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/a1d26e219b504c85ac732ff826edac3607ed7f5e1e0e614f6ae403b6153f37ff.png)

The proportions aren't too accurate to the image but I think it matches what I had in my vision pretty well! Onto the Jolteon :)

tl;dr is that I finished the jeep model, but it took me a lot of attempts because Blender couldn't undo my changes and I couldn't get my model to match the proportions I wanted.

### 2026-11-05: # starting jolteon :3

**1.4h**

# starting jolteon :3

Now that I'm done with the jeep, I can move on to creating my Jolteon! For this, I'll be using the sculpting tools in Blender, which, along with the normal Blender tools, I know absolutely nothing about.  And I don't have a guide for this one, since it's not too easy to tell someone exactly how to sculpt something. So I found this sort of tutorial just as an introduction to sculpting:

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Lxem4yMs5Dg

However, I found sculpting a bit more intuitive than just the modeling. It's definitely difficult, but I think I was able to get the general shape I wanted with sculpting. I started by creating an iso sphere and subdividing it, then just sculpting based off that. I also made sure to use the mirror tool, since I wanted to try making the head for now. After that, I also wanted a more low-poly look, so I remeshed it with a bigger grid. Since the head is basically just a sphere with a few edited features, it wasn't too difficult to make it match my reference. For the ears, I used a technique called "vertex modeling", where I just traced out the ears on my reference and extruded them out.

I also tried to do the same with the collar, but it doesn't really make sense to have it like a prism, so I pinched all the corners together.

![Screenshot 2026-11-04 231729](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/fed03354fa6c32535acb297ef1e45e43be5214c0f1355e193cc4b0f5cba1b7b2.png)

And this is basically just the final result! I'm super happy with it, and I'll be painting it when I get it printed!
![Screenshot 2026-11-04 235128](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/0d91cf2ae8121f9c94fd158eaebb91b7353dd7ef9cbb183df2a5955581386807.png)

### 2026-11-06: # modeling everything!

**2.4h**

# modeling everything!

Even though I do like the head that I made for my Jeepeon already, I kind of regret making it low-poly. It does match my reference image to some extent, but I think, with the smooth body of the jeep, it'd make more sense for the head to be smoother. So I spent a good while subdividing and re-sculpting some areas so that it'd match better with the new head. I still wanted it to be kind of low-poly, but just not in the way that I had it before. To do that, I just remeshed it with a voxel size of 0.6, and applied the same strategy to the other things I created. I also decided to switch everything to smooth shading, which I don't really know what it does, but it does make it look smoother! It kinda reminds me of those low-poly Pokemon models that were used in Rumble U, which I suppose the original reference image was based off of.

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 231808](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/64ddefabd016d9d6697573c1a6d76ef7f9e2202f86c9cf14e0a779ea3e2b624d.png)

I also added the spikes/fur to Jolteon's head, which I didn't before because I didn't know how :( After a little bit of research, I found you can poke a face and extrude it to create a spike, so I added that to the face, though that'd be nice to know earlier when I created the collar.

I also started working on the body, which was mostly made of iso spheres stretched and sculpted. I basically made the entire body by myself, so I'm super proud of it!! (this was before I decided to switch from low-poly, so that's why it looks like that). You can see how I used spheres to plan out each body part.

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 214133](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/f3c2832b54b1f9847c7dddff9947400c59b9b3b330874dbbc74f6a1fa5bededc.png)

For example, because I modeled the arms separate form the torso, the arms looked kind of weird attached to it? I can't really explain in words, but it did take a lot of tweaking with the grab and snake hook tool to try and get it to look right...

![Screenshot 2026-11-05 233408](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/9ebd50fd68ad70dcbe80b693dd1b09be6cd3b2b88655c4046bc93cee0d79a24a.png)

### 2026-11-06: # non-manifold nightmares

**1h**

# non-manifold nightmares

Now that I'm done my model I can get it ready for 3D-printing! I really only know that one of the biggest things you need to be able to print a model is that it has to be non-manifold, which means that there are no open gaps in the mesh. To check this, you just have to select all the non-manifold edges. I checked my Jolteon, which had no issues, but my jeep was a different story. Because my jeep was made using a mirror modifier, the gap in the center was an open face that was non-manifold, but I didn't realize this, so it basically just looked like a huge mess that was non-manifold.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/2b196a715956778f3a69db3744a9ea85fa3e83bec62d8b268470fc653c1f42c2.png)

Usually you fix manifold edges by just filling in the empty space, so I did that but it created this internal face that would probably create issues when 3D printing. It did fix the non-manifold edges though.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/cfa95c052100b23a0907b9b9bacad579bc895426ea16b7aa97f31d4c4f5c92ae.png)

It took a lot of time just searching it up to find out that I could just delete the edges and it'd all work out. I don't know why but it does and I'll leave it at that! :3

For some reason I also had other edges being non-manifold (it's the edge you see on the right side, unconnected from everything else), and I tried to fill those as well but it created the same problem of an interior face. So I just deleted them!

Turns out, though, there's some more factors you have to consider other than just the model being manifold, such as intersect faces and other stuff. To check this, I used the 3D print toolbox addon that Blender has, and I have a lot more stuff to fix than I thought...

So I probably should've made the model with the 3D-print-ability in mind, but I guess I can't go back now.

tl;dr is that I made everything manifold, but I have some other errors to fix

### 2026-11-08: # fixing every single error.

**2.8h**

# fixing every single error.

So as I said before in my previous entry, it's not just the non-manifold-ness that needs fixing, and there's a lot of other things. To see if your Blender model is ready for 3D printing, you can add the add-on 3D Print Toolbox, which identifies non-manifold edges, sharp edges, intersect faces, and other factors that'll make your model difficult to print, kind of like the DRC for KiCad. So here's all the errors that I had and how I fixed them! I mostly just researched a little bit, but there wasn't that much info, so a lot of it was just trial and error until the error goes away. Additionally, I had to fix all the errors for each of my parts, since the 3D Analyzer only checks for 1 part at a time. By far, the one part that took the longest was the Jeep, so that's why all the errors are based of that (but do note that I had to do it for ALL my parts, so that's why I spent so long on this)

(Reference of all my errors (bad))

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 201515](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/5d52af48e0dc868578064efde212f3ceaf5305e870d49f9edafd6c210e639766.png)

*Also another note, when fixing some errors, some other errors just popped up because of course they did. For example, when trying to fix my intersect faces, some edges would become non-manifold, and then I'd have to fix that too, so it was just a loop of fixing and fixing...

##  Intersect Faces
As said in the previous entry, I fixed basically all the non-manifold errors (yay!) and bad contiguous errors I never had to deal with, but I always had a lot of intersect faces. These are faces that, as it explains, intersect with other faces, which can be a problem because your 3D printer doesn't know whether to count those faces as faces or just being inside of another face.

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 202507](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/9e53943665232982c69cc65b5fa9c6102aab82ef3b4697f3e4fa23f3e216c10f.png)
(this is an example with the rear-view mirror)

 I thought it'd be easy to fix using a boolean modifier and union, which would just combine everything into one part so they aren't intersecting anymore. I made my Jeep with the idea that I would just unify everything together into one part anyways, kinda like what I did in Onshape for my Fishbl. However, this didn't work because it would count the face that was made by unifying the two parts together as an intersect face itself.

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 203241](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/6e5c24d0257573c313c0880f096b4154b7fca58c775b8a03a109f9c0d1650cf7.png)

I could NOT figure out how to fix this no matter how hard I tried. I tried just deleting the face, but that would create non-manifold edges. I tried deleting the non-manifold edges, but that would create even MORE non-manifold edges. I also tried merging the arm and the mirror together, but then it wouldn't even look like a rear-view mirror. So I eventually compromised and just moved it into a seperate mesh entirely. I was planning to slice it anyways in Bambu Studio, since it would be difficult to print such a small part overhanging attached to a larger part, and it'd just be easier to print it separately and glue it on.

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 202355](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/e6335bff43453dcdf3fd7cbdd2b6d0ac3b955528f41eff96b442bfdb2ba43caf.png)

Another major area I had the intersect faces issue was in the car wheels. I'm pretty sure the tutorial I used for modeling the car was meant for video game model usage, not 3D printing, so I didn't realize that it wouldn't be okay. I originally tried to fix this by moving the wheels out a little bit so they aren't intersecting with the car, but I was afraid they wouldn't be actually attached to each other (I tried using snapping as well, but it didn't work because it would snap to the center of the wheel rather than the edge and also just didn't look right), so I used the same strategy as the rear-view mirrors by separating them into another mesh.

Basically I thought the boolean union was a good idea (I did use it when fixing other errors), but it creates way too many non-manifold edges that are way too difficult to fix anyways. I also used the same strategy for the windshield and now that's separate too. Because they're now all separate parts, I also had to fix the errors created when I made the part.

## Zero Faces
Zero faces are "faces" in a model that have an area of zero. I don't even know how you even create that, nor do I know why I have 5.

![zerofaces](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/9c371c4c02f1eaf30c0651df8871d9dfb572ee024851aec57da3ca8929e6f45d.png)

That's also clearly 6 "faces" labeled, not 5. But I digress.

Anyways, the main problem with these edges was the bevel I made for the main edges of the trapezoid-shaped part of the car, and that it didn't align with the rectangle-shaped part of the car (as it didn't have a bevel). Of course, how was I even to know this at all?? I tried to delete the faces (because what's the point of having the faces if they don't even have an area) but apparently they function like connecting points and create non-manifold edges when I delete them. Instead, I merged together the bevel area, so it basically doesn't even have a bevel anymore. Why do I even try.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/2bb6247e69edaa25d284f7ab413ffc4f3330a1d3855d793a0b14e54aadc2ba27.png)

## Non-Flat Faces
Non-flat faces are self-explanatory. Faces that are not flat. It doesn't really sound that bad to me, but it was pretty easy to fix anyways. All you have to do is triangulate all your faces, which can either be done using ctrl+t or using a triangulate modifier. BambuStudio will triangulate the faces anyways (as it can only read triangles), but I like seeing 0 errors so I just fixed it in Blender.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/6a89f9123727aad9aaa5fccfd42045105c87a0249deba37816d952ed22083134.png)

## Shells
Shells are the different "parts" of your mesh, or basically the meshes that don't connect together. I don't know why I had 14, but I managed to get it into 1 (as the car is only meant to be 1 part, printed entirely on its own).

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/2f3480dedbf685c0152604fbc66998735f6bf420c53d513f4db7cbb8249ab768.png)

So I fixed the car!

## Extra
Here's some more errors I had that aren't dealing with the car:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/5becd7a4c35f35a04757c9c69bf6db4f0001119843c75d70dbc227aae705d8a3.png)

I remodeled the ears because they were too sharp and pointy (too many thin faces, sharp edges) that would probably be difficult for a printer to print, even if it has a thin nozzle. So I just extruded instead, and smoothed it out so it's easier to print.

![Screenshot 2026-11-06 225031](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/418dea17a9947a3f5df2b35ced14036ee5453841beab05b78a8e06f54676587d.png)
The original steering wheel I made didn't keep non-manifold edges or intersecting faces in mind. I tried to fix it, but I realized it'd probably be easier just to remodel it instead. To make it, I just created a cylinder, used a boolean modifier to take out the center, and bridge opposite faces together to make an X shape.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/c572b554b9c7bd4f798a615d06f267d8be9be3a2029df9faeded52a6ab48f30c.png)
I also slightly remodeled/resculpted the torso, since the arms and main body were seperate shells, and there were too many sharp edges (so I smoothed it all out).

tl;dr is that I fixed all the errors with all the parts in my design, including non-manifold edges, intersect faces, shells, zero faces, non-flat faces, thin faces, and sharp edges

### 2026-11-08: # slicing!

**0.3h**

# slicing!

So one thing I didn't keep in mind when making my model was the scale into the real world. This is mostly because CAD requires actual measurements, but Blender doesn't, and I basically made mine as if it was a video game model instead of an actually 3D printable model. When I tried exporting it into a 3mf and importing that into Bambu Studio to slice it, it turned out looking like this:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/4b01bea2468f62666cef909a584f11212e27ff9eeee4cbee587869dc6f5b2cca.png)

Basically it's so huge that you can't even see the build plate. It was essentially 4m long, which is way too big for a small figure. So I joined together all my objects in Blender and scaled them altogether (since scaling them separately scaled on each of their own origins), and then imported the fixed 3mf into Bambu Studio.

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/f3042eaa63fc92a1272f59e300fde0bc200ce479e57f877122f1502ee9cbd439.png)

It's a pretty small print so I'm hoping it'll be cheap!

I also generated supports:

![image](https://halflife.hackclub-assets.com/sessions/Fkyd7BnPhA7YS61rynMPOy9Dgjdve6I4/f2e64595bd0f1048fd45301bdd0412321f50a6bf532a1cf28b8d716119e1e7fb.png)

tl;dr is that I got my 3mf into BambuStudio to generate supports, but it was way too big so I had to scale it down
